Job Description

The Opportunity


Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University is seeking an Academic Advisor to support student success, retention, and degree completion by providing personalized academic guidance and exceptional student service. The Academic Advisor serves as a trusted resource for students throughout their academic journey, from admission through graduation, by helping students navigate degree requirements, academic policies, registration processes, and university resources.


This role provides an opportunity to make a meaningful impact by building relationships with students, developing individualized academic plans, identifying barriers to success, and connecting students with campus resources that support their educational goals. The Academic Advisor collaborates with faculty and university departments to promote student engagement, persistence, and overall academic achievement.


Key Responsibilities


Academic Advising & Student Success


  • Provide comprehensive academic advising to students regarding degree programs, curriculum requirements, academic policies, procedures, transfer credits, prerequisites, graduation requirements, and interpretation of Official Advising Reports.
  • Develop personalized degree completion plans and guide students through course selection, registration, and academic planning to support timely graduation.
  • Monitor student academic progress throughout enrollment terms and provide proactive outreach, guidance, and intervention when challenges arise.
  • Advise students regarding program changes, academic petitions, curriculum waivers, catalog changes, graduation applications, and other academic requests.
  • Provide individualized support to at-risk students, including those on conditional admission, academic warning, or probation, by developing student success plans and monitoring progress.
  • Collaborate with faculty and university departments to address academic challenges and support student retention and persistence.
  • Promote institutional initiatives, scholarships, financial aid opportunities, honor societies, career resources, and student engagement programs.

Student Outreach & Engagement


  • Proactively communicate with students through phone, email, text/chat, and virtual meetings to provide guidance and promote student success.
  • Contact students throughout their academic journey, including newly admitted students, enrolled students, inactive students, and graduating students.
  • Welcome newly admitted students by providing information on degree requirements, enrollment steps, financial resources, orientation, and required university tasks.
  • Conduct regular student outreach to assess academic progress, address concerns, and identify resources needed for successful course completion.
  • Encourage student participation in advising appointments, university services, and engagement opportunities.
  • Support student transitions by congratulating graduates, recognizing academic achievements, and promoting alumni and university engagement opportunities.

Student Records & Administrative Support


  • Maintain accurate student records and documentation within university systems, including Campus Solutions, Salesforce, SharePoint, Imaging, and other applicable platforms.
  • Document advising interactions, student progress, and action plans through detailed advisor notes.
  • Analyze student academic records to identify enrollment concerns, degree progression issues, and opportunities for intervention.
  • Evaluate prerequisite completion and ensure students are meeting curriculum requirements.
  • Manage an assigned student caseload while supporting enrollment goals and student persistence initiatives.
  • Prepare and review student reports, track academic trends, and contribute data insights related to retention and student success.
  • Provide coverage and support for team members’ student caseloads as needed.
  • Serve as a liaison between students and university offices, including Financial Aid, Military and Veteran Affairs, Student Financial Services, the Registrar, Bookstore, and other support departments.

About us


For nearly 100 years, Embry-Riddle has been the world's leading aviation and aerospace university, educating more than 30,000 students across residential campuses in Daytona Beach, Florida, and Prescott, Arizona, as well as through a global network of Worldwide locations and online programs. With more than 165,000 alumni around the world, our impact reaches every corner of the aerospace, aviation, defense and technology industries.


Today, our faculty, researchers and professional staff are advancing innovation across aviation, space, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, autonomous systems and next-generation engineering. Working alongside industry leaders, government agencies and innovators, they are solving real-world challenges and shaping the technologies that will define tomorrow.


Whether you are an educator, researcher, administrator, technologist or industry professional, your work at Embry-Riddle will contribute to something bigger than a job. Join a community driven by discovery, purpose and excellence—and help shape the future of aerospace.


  • Generous Time Off: Enjoy up to 18 days of paid leave in your first year, including 3 days granted upon hire and 15 days accrued throughout the year. You'll also receive 9+ paid holidays, including the day after Thanksgiving and the week between Christmas Eve and New Year's Day.
  • Tuition Coverage: Get 100% tuition coverage for yourself for one undergraduate and one graduate degree, and discounted rates for your spouse and dependent children up to age 26.
  • Retirement Contributions: ERAU contributes 6% of your base salary to your retirement plan and offers a 4% matching contribution – with no vesting period.
  • Personal Leave: Relax with 15 days of personal leave for non-exempt employees or 18 days for exempt full-time employees in your first year.

Compensation

The annual salary range for this role is up to $43,888. The final offer will be based on the candidate’s skills, qualifications, and experience, as well as applicable state regulations, internal equity, and business needs, and may fall outside of the stated range.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
  • 1–3 years of related work experience in student support, academic advising, student services, higher education, or a related field.
  • Experience providing guidance, support, or customer service to students or other stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze information, identify solutions, and make informed decisions using sound judgment.
  • Experience working with student information systems and maintaining accurate records.

Required Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities


  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret student records, academic information, policies, and procedures.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook/email, and internet-based end-user applications.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate with students, faculty, staff, and other university stakeholders.
  • Strong customer service skills with the ability to provide a high level of support to students, colleagues, faculty, and other constituents.
  • Ability to establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with supervisors, managers, team members, and university partners.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and maintain attention to detail.
  • Comfortable conducting frequent proactive outreach and communication with students and stakeholders through phone, email, text/chat, and virtual meetings.
  • Ability to recognize priorities, take initiative, perform duties beyond assigned tasks when needed, and provide support to team members.
  • Ability to quickly learn new systems, processes, and technologies while adapting to changing environments.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to investigate issues, identify appropriate solutions, and take corrective action.
  • Ability to maintain a positive, professional, and student-focused approach in all interactions.
  • Ability to handle challenging situations tactfully, maintain composure under pressure, and demonstrate professionalism.
  • Ability to seek guidance and direction when appropriate while working independently.
  • Ability to exercise good judgment and make sound decisions in support of student success.

Location: Remote, United States.

Reports to: Sam Levine, Chief Product Officer.

Start date: January 2027 (March at the latest).

About Breathe for Change

Breathe for Change is building the category of Human Intelligence in Education to address the crises of educator stress and burnout, student mental health, and AI disruption. Our accredited higher-education program, a Master of Science in Education in Transformative Teaching & Learning awarded by William Jewell College and accredited by the Higher Learning Commission, equips educators with the human skills they and their students need most to thrive. More than 20,000 educators in every U.S. state have come through our programs.

The role

As an Academic Advisor and Professor, you’ll support educators throughout their experience in our master’s program, both in their courses and through individual guidance and mentorship.

  • As an advisor, you’ll get to know students and their goals, help them navigate challenges, and reach out when they need extra support.

  • As a professor, you’ll teach courses, guide their action research, and offer meaningful feedback that helps them grow. Working with students in both ways will also give you valuable insight into how we can continue improving the program.

As our program grows, we want every student to feel known, supported, and connected to their learning. You’ll play an important part in making that happen, helping working educators balance their studies with the demands of their lives and keep moving toward graduation. Success in this role will center on student engagement, retention, and ultimately graduation from the program.

Our students are educators first

Our students are balancing their studies with their work in schools, their families, and the many demands of daily life. A thoughtful check-in can make a real difference. As an advisor, you’ll build relationships that help you recognize when students need support, reach out with care, and help them find a way forward.

We’re a small team with a shared purpose

You’ll work closely with our founders, Chief Product Officer, curriculum team, and fellow faculty to support our students and strengthen the program. We value your ideas and experience, and you’ll have opportunities to help shape our approach to advising. We also use AI tools in our work and encourage you to explore how they can support thoughtful, effective teaching and student support.

We honor the trust educators place in us

Pursuing a degree is a meaningful investment of time, energy, and money. Our students deserve clear, accurate information about their courses, credits, timelines, and pathways so they can make informed decisions. You’ll help us honor that trust by offering reliable guidance, following through on commitments, and helping students understand what to expect throughout the program.

What you’ll do

  • Guide and support 200–300 students. Serve as their primary academic contact throughout the program, offering guidance on coursework, academic progress, and action research capstone projects. Help students choose pathways, courses, and focus areas that connect with their goals.

  • Help students stay connected and on track. Use our student dashboard to recognize changes in engagement and progress, and reach out early when someone may need support. Through individual check-ins, coaching, and follow-through, you’ll help students work through challenges and make steady progress toward graduation.

  • Teach and mentor educators. Lead courses in our master’s program, including Human Intelligence, specialty courses in areas such as mental health and trauma, and the practicum sequence. Create engaging learning experiences and offer thoughtful feedback that helps students deepen their understanding and apply what they’re learning in their communities.

  • Help strengthen the student experience. Share what you learn through advising and teaching with our curriculum and student experience teams. Your insights and ideas will help us improve our courses, strengthen advising, and better support educators throughout the program.

Who we’re looking for

Required qualifications

  • A master’s degree in education. An EdD or PhD is a strong plus.

  • Experience conducting action research at the master’s or doctoral level. You’ve designed and completed a rigorous action research project and can share it with us.

  • Experience facilitating online learning. You’ve led live or asynchronous trainings or courses and bring both strong content knowledge and an ability to make learning engaging and accessible.

Experience we especially value

  • Classroom teaching. You understand the joys and challenges of working in schools firsthand.

  • Advising, mentoring, or coaching. You’ve helped learners or educators work toward their goals and navigate challenges along the way.

  • Expertise in social-emotional learning, mindfulness, or transformational work. You bring experience in areas that are central to our degree programs.

What you’ll bring to the team

  • Care and initiative. You build relationships with students, notice when someone may be struggling, and reach out. You can manage a large advising caseload while staying attentive to individual needs.

  • Comfort using data to guide support. You’re comfortable using dashboards, engagement scores, and Hubspot to organize your work and identify students who may need a check-in. You pair that information with conversations that help you understand each student’s experience.

  • Warm, clear communication. Much of our advising happens in writing. You communicate in ways that help students feel supported, understand their next steps, and feel comfortable asking for help.

Our hiring process

We’ll begin with a 30-minute conversation with our Chief Product Officer to learn about your experience and share more about the role. Next, you’ll lead a 20-minute facilitation demo for members of our faculty, followed by 10 minutes of feedback and conversation. You’ll then meet with one of our academic advisors to talk through how you’d support students, and we’ll close with a final conversation with our Chief Product Officer. Each conversation is a chance for you to get to know us, too.

Compensation & benefits

  • Base salary of $110,000–$130,000 for US-based candidates, depending on experience

  • Annual performance bonus

  • Stock options

  • Health, vision, and dental insurance

  • 401(k) and FSA/HSA eligibility

  • Unlimited paid time off

How to apply

We’d love to learn about you through your teaching, your research, and your interest in supporting educators. In addition to your résumé, please share these three important parts of your application:

  • A 5-10 minute video of you facilitating learning, whether recorded for asynchronous learning, in person, or on Zoom.

  • Your action research project, such as a capstone, thesis, or dissertation.

  • Why you’re excited about this role and what would help you succeed in it. Tell us about the experiences, strengths, and interests you’d bring to our students and team.

Breathe for Change is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Compensation Range: $110K - $130K

About ICL Academy

A new model of private online education: Connecting academics, student passions, and industry experts. ICL Academy is an online private school for grades 5-12 that aims to solve many problems facing in-person and online schools by focusing on student engagement through a personalized, blended approach that combines academics with personal passions. Its founder, Kirk Spahn, is a fourth-generation educator with over 20 years of experience specializing in digital education and youth civic engagement. ICL Academy is powered by 150 years of academic excellence. It builds on the track record of success of the Institute for Civic Leadership, a nonprofit founded in 2001 that has inspired, educated, and supported a new generation of youth civic leaders to take positive action in their local and global communities.

ICL Academy also partners with industry experts who serve as master teachers and Champion Mentors. ICL Academy is grateful to have amazing Champions such as Novak Djokovic, Steve Nash, Bode Miller, Monica Seles, Vincent Zhou, and so many more supporting its community of students and families. ICL Academy has quickly become the #1 online school for kids pursuing their passion.

Position Summary:

We seek a highly motivated, experienced professional to join the ICL Academy team as an Academic Advisor & Student Support Specialist. Reporting to the Dean of Counseling & Advising, this position plays an important role in supporting students and families throughout the admissions, academic planning, and enrollment process while maintaining a small caseload of ICL students.

The Academic Advisor & Student Support Specialist will partner closely with the Admissions, Academic Advising, Records, and instructional teams to review student transcripts and prior coursework, evaluate transferable credits, develop individualized four-year academic plans, and identify appropriate academic supports. This position will also oversee the review and documentation of 504 Plans, IEPs, and other accommodation-related documentation provided during enrollment and will collaborate with the Head of School, ICL Teachers, and Academic Advisors to support the implementation of appropriate accommodations within ICL’s flexible learning model.

As a member of the Academic Advising team, this position will develop meaningful relationships with students and families within their caseload and provide individualized academic planning, student support, and guidance throughout the student’s enrollment at ICL. The Academic Advisor & Student Support Specialist will also serve as a resource to the broader Academic Advising team on matters related to accommodations and other complex student support needs.

Job Duties and Responsibilities:

Admissions Academic Review & Course Planning:

  • Partner with the Admissions and Records teams to conduct academic reviews for prospective ICL Students in grades 5-12.
  • Review and evaluate student transcripts, academic records, and prior coursework to determine appropriate credit transfer and remaining graduation requirements.
  • Develop individualized four-year academic plans for incoming high school students that reflect transferred credits, current-year course placement, graduation requirements, and projected course planning through senior year.
  • Identify potential academic gaps, credit deficiencies, course sequencing considerations, or other academic factors that may impact a student’s pathway toward graduation. Work in collaboration with the Head of Admissions, Head of School, and Registrar on more complex individual transcript reviews and course planning.
  • Communicate academic findings and recommendations to the Admissions team to support informed enrollment and course placement decisions.
  • Partner with the Academic Advising team to ensure a smooth transition from the admissions process into ongoing academic advising.
  • Maintain accurate academic review documentation and four-year plans within the appropriate student information systems.

504, IEP, Psych-Ed Evaluations & Accommodation Support:

  • Review 504 Plans, IEPs, Psych-Ed Evaluations, and other educational support documentation provided during the admissions and enrollment process, or after enrollment.
  • Identify documented accommodations and determine their applicability within ICL Academy’s flexible instructional model.
  • Document relevant student support information and create and maintain ICL Accommodation Plan when applicable.
  • Maintain accurate and confidential records related to student accommodations and educational support needs.
  • Partner with Head of School, Academic Advisors and ICL Teachers to communicate and clarify student accommodations and support their appropriate implementation.
  • Collaborate with the Head of School and the Dean of Counseling & Advising when requested accommodations fall outside the scope of ICL’s flexible program and require additional consideration or support.
  • Partner with the Academic Advising team when students or families request testing accommodations for the ACT, SAT, or other standardized assessments.
  • Assist with the review and coordination of documentation required for standardized testing accommodations, as appropriate.

Student Advising & Support:

  • Maintain a small caseload of approximately 60 students and develop individualized, supportive relationships with students and families.
  • Serve as a consistent academic and student support resource for students within the Advisor’s caseload.
  • Monitor academic progress and proactively identify students who may benefit from additional academic, organizational, or school-based support.
  • Support students with academic planning, course selection, graduation requirements, goal setting, and post-secondary planning.
  • Maintain accurate and updated four-year plans for students within the Advisor’s caseload, incorporating transferred credits, current coursework, graduation requirements, and post-secondary goals.
  • Demonstrate knowledge of the National Collegiate Athletics Association (NCAA) eligibility guidelines and the University of California (UC) admissions requirements.
  • Guide a small number of senior students (if and when 12th graders are on the Advisor’s caseload) and their families in all aspects of the college admissions planning process, including the development of the college list, standardized testing, timing of applications, college essays, letters of recommendation, and financial aid and scholarships.
  • Collaborate with teachers, Academic Advisors, and families to develop appropriate strategies and supports for students experiencing academic challenges.
  • Support students with organization, time management, goal setting, and other executive functioning skills as appropriate.
  • Serve as a resource to Academic Advisors regarding accommodations, and other or student support matters including testing accommodations for the ACT/SAT..etc.
  • Refer students with significant academic, social-emotional, or mental health concerns to the Dean of Counseling & Advising or other appropriate resources.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date student records, including relevant academic, student support, and accommodation information.
  • Support student retention by proactively communicating with students and families and collaborating with the broader student support team.

Collaboration & School Support:

  • Work collaboratively with the Head of School, Dean of Counseling & Advising, Academic Advising, Admissions, Records, and instructional teams to support the academic success and well-being of ICL students.
  • Liaise with the Records and Academic Advising team as needed to ensure accuracy of student transcripts, credits, academic records, and graduation plans.
  • Participate/Lead in collaboration and student support meetings as appropriate.
  • Support the development and refinement of school-wide processes related to accommodations and student support.
  • Support and participate in key virtual webinars, orientations, and other programming designed to support students’ and families’ transition to ICL.
  • Participate in school-wide retention efforts and strategies.
  • In partnership with the Director of Community Engagement, support student and family engagement through participation in appropriate community-building events.
  • Support the planning and implementation of the school’s annual year-end celebration.
  • Attend the annual year-end celebration.
  • Additional duties as assigned.

Job Requirements, Skills, and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • Graduate degree in school counseling or academic advising strongly preferred.
  • Experience working with 504 Plans, IEPs, and/or student accommodations strongly preferred.
  • College admissions experience, at either the college or high school levels, preferred.
  • Tutoring and/or academic advising experience preferred.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound professional judgment when working with sensitive student information.
  • Familiarity with ACT and SAT testing accommodation processes preferred.
  • Technologically proficient in student information systems required.
  • Highly organized.
  • Outstanding interpersonal and community relations skills and the ability to communicate and work effectively within a diverse community.
  • Ability to foster a cooperative work environment.
  • A professional who operates with ethics and integrity.
  • High degree of flexibility.
  • Demonstrated ability to work well in a fast-paced environment.

Benefits:

  • Sponsored Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits
  • Sponsored 401K Plan
  • Sponsored $50K Life Insurance included for all employees
  • Flexible PTO
  • Remote/Work from Home and flexible hours
  • Professional development

About Inspira Education

Inspira Education Group is one of the fastest-growing edtech startups in the US. We started with a simple mission to democratize access to high-quality coaching so that every student in the world has an equal opportunity to access the best opportunities.

As the world’s leading network of top admissions coaches in medical, legal, business, and college studies, we’re building software and services in one place—disrupting long-entrenched application processes with products and experiences that strive to provide an equal platform for candidates from diverse backgrounds worldwide.

As one of the fastest-growing edtech firms in the world, we are backed by some of the leading venture capital firms and investors in the world, including Zeev Ventures, Quiet Capital, Craft Ventures and Jeff Fluhr (Founder of Stubhub).

The Role

We’re currently hiring Senior Academic Advisors across multiple Inspira Education Group brands.

We’re looking for a driven, entrepreneurial Senior Academic Advisor with a strong ownership mindset. Someone who thrives in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment and is eager to help students achieve their academic dreams. You’ll play a key role in driving revenue growth through inbound sales, while also helping to build and refine the systems and processes that will allow our sales function to scale in the future.

This is one of the most impactful roles at Inspira. As the first point of contact for parents and students exploring our programs, you’ll set the tone for their entire experience. The trust, empathy, and expertise you bring to these conversations often become the deciding factors in their choice to work with us. You’ll guide them through one of the most meaningful decisions of their lives- investing in their education and future success.

What You'll Do

  • Lead consultative intro calls (inbound) with parents and students to understand their goals, explain the admissions process, and recommend the right Inspira programs and packages based on their needs
  • Own the relationship with prospective students and families from first touch through enrollment by building trust, offering guidance, and ensuring a smooth and positive experience throughout their journey
  • Follow up strategically and consistently to stay connected with prospects, anticipate questions or concerns, and help them confidently decide to partner with Inspira
  • Experiment and innovate—test new scripts, refine messaging, and explore creative follow-up strategies to maximize conversion rates and continuously improve the enrollment experience
  • Close deals across a range of programs and services, meeting or exceeding monthly and quarterly sales goals
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with the marketing, counseling, and finance teams to ensure seamless handoffs, strong alignment, and an exceptional customer experience
  • Stay informed on competitor offerings and market trends; provide real-time feedback to founders and leadership to shape product, pricing, and go-to-market strategy
  • Leverage HubSpot CRM to manage the full sales cycle—tracking leads, logging communications, creating email templates, forecasting revenue, and maintaining data integrity across all stages
  • Forecast enrollments accurately by managing deal stages, values, and close dates in HubSpot
  • Support onboarding and customer success for newly enrolled students to ensure a strong start and high satisfaction

Who You Are

  • 3–5 years of experience in inbound sales within a service-oriented or consultative environment, ideally with sales cycles under 2–3 months
  • Proven success selling premium or high-value service packages (ACV $5,000+), with a track record of exceeding targets and delivering exceptional client experiences
  • Excellent communication skills. You’re confident presenting, writing, and speaking with clarity, empathy, and professionalism
  • Strong CRM proficiency, preferably in HubSpot (or similar tools), with a knack for maintaining clean data and using systems to drive performance
  • Comfort with data and reporting, including experience using Excel or Google Sheets to build and interpret dashboards
  • Nice to Have: Prior experience in education, admissions, or academic consulting sales

What We Value

As a fast-growing startup, every team member plays a pivotal role in shaping our culture and driving our success. At Inspira, we’re looking for people who embody these core values:

  • Winning Attitude: You find a way to succeed. You dig deeper to understand the “why” behind a no, and you don’t stop until you’ve found a solution
  • Curiosity: You constantly push yourself to learn, experiment, and improve. You’re open to new ideas and you see setbacks as opportunities to grow
  • Genuine Relationships: You lead with empathy and integrity. Parents and students trust us with one of the most important decisions of their lives, and you honor that by building authentic, human connections
  • Smart and Hard Work: You combine awareness and judgment with effort and discipline. You know when to think strategically and when to roll up your sleeves
  • Humility and Teamwork: You celebrate collective success over individual wins. You welcome feedback, learn from mistakes, and support those around you

Why you'll love Inspira

  • Amazing people with a great vision and values
  • Mission-driven team culture focused on student success

The SSA guides and assists CAGS students toward successful degree completion and attainment of educational goals. This position is a key component in the retention and persistence of students.

While the campus is in Lakewood, CAGS students are located in varying regions both inside and outside of Colorado. As a result, this position requires high levels of accurate and concise communication (email, phone, and in-person, depending on the student’s location).

A polished, professional demeanor is required. Hours may vary depending on student need and may include evenings and weekends.

Job Location

Remote - must reside and work legally in the U.S. All work must be performed within the U.S.

About CCU

Colorado Christian University is the premier interdenominational Christian university in Colorado and the Rocky Mountain region, delivering world class education to thousands of students. The fully accredited, nonprofit University is located in Lakewood, Colorado, a suburb of Denver.

Colorado Christian University was founded in 1914. CCU’s motto is--grace and truth. This motto comes from John 1.14: “And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory as of the only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.” (ESV)

CCU's mission is Christ-centered higher education transforming students to impact the world with grace and truth.

Colorado Christian University cultivates knowledge and love of God in a Christ-centered community of learners and scholars, with an enduring commitment to the integration of exemplary academics, spiritual formation, and engagement with the world. We envision graduates who think critically and creatively, lead with high ethical and professional standards, embody the character and compassion of Jesus Christ, treasure the gospel, and who thereby are prepared to impact the world in their callings.

CCU embraces an educational model that was present at the foundation of many of the great western and American universities. It is made up of three pillars—competence, character and Christ-centered faith. Secular universities have abandoned two of those pillars. We think this is a major oversight that eventually undermines education. Furthermore, we believe this classical educational model is both life-giving and greatly needed in our time.

A leader in higher education, CCU has been consistently ranked in the top 2 percent of colleges and universities nationwide for its core curriculum by the American Council of Trustees and Alumni. CCU has had ten consecutive years of enrollment growth and has been named one of the five fastest-growing master’s granting universities by The Chronicle of Higher Education.

CCU offers more than 200 degree program options for traditional and adult students through its two colleges--the College of Undergraduate Studies and College of Adult and Graduate Studies. More than 9,000 students attend the University on the main campus, in regional centers throughout Colorado, and online.

  1. Faith-friendly: CCU’s culture is unique to higher education. Where else can you pursue academic excellence yet read the Holy Bible, pray with teammates and students at work, and work to impact our culture in support of Christian values?
  2. Convictionally Christian: As a university, we have an enduring commitment to Christ, his kingdom and the truth of God’s Word.
  3. Live out your calling: We are a traditional evangelical university where you can invest your God-given talents and abilities alongside coworkers and teammates, while having a profound influence on students as they deepen their relationship with Jesus Christ.
  4. Equip students for kingdom work: You can be a part of helping students discover their callings and preparing them for positions of significant leadership in the church, business, government, education, and other professions, as a key part of our University's Strategic Priorities.

  1. High technology proficiency; fluency in Microsoft Excel and Outlook.
  2. Confidence with a high level of inbound/outbound calls; proven ability to articulate clearly and persuasively, yet professionally, with students.
  3. Self-confidence, patience, empathy, and availability when building rapport with students; ability to understand and adapt quickly to multi-generational needs and characteristics.

  6. Consistently cohesive working relationships, ability to view conflict positively and operate with honesty and respect in all communication.
  7. Disposition to enjoy a high-energy call center-type work environment, maintain focus amidst unexpected distractions, and manage disruptions with professionalism.

  6. Partner strategically with other departments to facilitate and process time-sensitive student requests.
  7. Prepare and plan for future blocks/semesters; collaborate with colleagues on special projects; attend team meetings and training webinars/conference calls.

Role Summary

The Academic Counselor partners with students and families in grades 7-12 to support academic success, graduation completion, and postsecondary readiness. Academic Counselors focus on high-impact, student-facing work, academic decision-making, graduation oversight, postsecondary planning, and whole-child academic support - while collaborating closely with Advisors, Student Support Specialists, Teachers, and the Registrar.

Academic Counselors are expected to spend approximately 45–50% of their work week (18–20 hours per week) in direct and indirect student-facing activities, including student and family meetings, academic planning conversations, proactive outreach, and intervention.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

Academic Planning & Graduation Oversight

  • Develop and maintain individualized academic plans aligned to graduation requirements and student goals

  • Monitor academic progress toward graduation and intervene when students fall off track

  • Lead student-specific graduation pathway planning and course sequencing decisions

  • Ensure students meet graduation eligibility requirements

Student Intervention & Case Management

  • Serve as the primary Tier 2 intervention point for students escalated by Advisors

  • Conduct targeted counseling conversations to identify barriers to academic progress

  • Develop and implement short-term academic intervention plans

  • Coordinate support across Advisors, Student Support Specialists, Teachers, and administrative teams

  • Monitor intervention outcomes and adjust plans as needed

  • Hold firm boundaries around academic policy and eligibility requirements when needed, while keeping the conversation supportive and counselor-forward

Student & Family Engagement

  • Build and maintain strong, trust-based relationships with students and families

  • Facilitate proactive and responsive parent–student–counselor meetings

  • Serve as a consistent point of contact for complex academic planning conversations

  • Communicate clearly and collaboratively to support student persistence

Postsecondary Planning & Curriculum Alignment

  • Guide students and families in postsecondary planning, including college, career, and alternative pathways

  • Provide accurate guidance on graduation requirements and future readiness

Onboarding & Enrollment

  • Partner with the Registrar to ensure accurate records review, course placement and scheduling execution

  • Support students through key transitions, including entry, re-entry, and graduation

Whole-Child Academic Perspective

  • Apply a whole-child lens to academic planning, recognizing external factors that impact learning and engagement

  • Integrate wellness considerations into academic decision-making without providing clinical mental health treatment

  • Support students in developing self-advocacy, goal-setting, and executive functioning skills

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for mental health-related concerns escalated by staff: assess academic impact, develop a support plan, and refer to internal or external resources as needed — while holding a firm boundary against providing therapy, ongoing counseling, or diagnosis

Student Safety & Compliance

  • Provide consultation and academic follow-up after safety protocols are enacted

  • develop a strong working relationship with the college advisor, acting as a unified team that will support the applicant through the application process
